subject: FDA Tobacco Marketing Granted Orders Enforcement
overview: The Medford Board of Health reviewed food safety and housing code violations, updated local heating season dates, and voted to maintain a May 1st enforcement deadline for tobacco products lacking FDA marketing granted orders.

items.title: Lighthouse Cafe Food Safety Compliance
items.summary: The board reviewed repeated food safety violations at Lighthouse Cafe and recommended the business retain a food safety consultant to assist with staff certification and operational procedures.

items.title: Property Complaint - 552 Main Street
items.summary: Health department staff reviewed rodent and bird-feeding complaints at 552 Main Street, where the homeowner explained the property is currently listed for sale and agreed to comply with local wildlife feeding rules.

items.title: Heating Season Designation
items.summary: Approved designating the annual heating season to end no earlier than May 15th and resume no later than September 30th.

items.title: Housing Code Violations - 57 Edward Street
items.summary: The board reviewed an order to correct citing 31 housing code violations and directed health inspectors to conduct an updated safety inspection of the unit before deciding whether to issue an order to vacate.

items.title: Communicable Disease Report
items.summary: The board received an update on April communicable disease trends and noted that Alpha-gal syndrome has officially become a reportable condition in Massachusetts.

items.title: FDA Tobacco Marketing Granted Orders Enforcement
items.summary: Local tobacco retailers and industry representatives requested an extension on enforcement against selling vapes and nicotine pouches without FDA marketing granted orders, but the board voted to keep the May 1st deadline intact.
